item.title: BU fraternity members face legal battles, lack of University support
item.description: Five Boston University social fraternities said they are facing legal battles against the Boston Police Department as a result of large-scale social gatherings that escalated to court cases against students living in the houses where the events occurred, according to court dockets and interviews with fraternity members.

item.description: The internet is not a safe place. Harmful subject matter such as nonconsensual records of nudity and, in extreme cases, child sexual abuse material, gets shared across the internet — and even ends up on the AI models trained to flag it. item.title: In groundbreaking study, BU’s CTE center links CTE with dementia and not behavioral problems
item.description: Some of the traditionally associated symptoms of chronic traumatic encephalopathy —a degenerative brain disease most attributed with football and other contact sports — include depression, aggressive behavior, memory loss and even suicidal thoughts. But a recent study from Boston University’s CTE Center just added another feature to the list: dementia.

item.title: BU law students fight for second chances for incarcerated women through Defender Clinic
item.description: Law students are often depicted in movies spending all their time poring over textbooks and studying for intense exams. Law students at Boston University help convicted women get a “second chance at freedom” in the courtroom.

item.title: How much money can we make off of mental health? | Data Driven
item.description: Social media and technology sometimes feels like this ambiguously large and evil boogeyman that grew out of control. I don’t think we could have ever guessed the consequences, and I worry that we won’t be able to control it now that it is so mainstream and infiltrated in our lives.

item.title: The hidden price of hustle culture | Editorial
item.description: Universities may not manufacture burnout deliberately, but they operate comfortably within the ecosystem that produces it. High internship and job placement rates strengthen rankings, successful alumni reinforce prestige and career outcomes drive admissions marketing — especially when university status is directly linked to future career opportunities. While burnout is unfortunate for students, the culture of relentless achievement undeniably sustains institutional status.
